title: fix(metadata-protocol): the read naming no package serves the row the package-less save writes, beside a package-unbound row (S6)
body:
Fixes #23291
Clause-②: no

## Option chosen: (c), the read naming no package resolves the address the save resolves

The triage (`6149653063`) asked the lane to pick one of three options under ADR-0070 TL;DR 1 and say why. This PR takes **(c)**.

`ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getMetaItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) now picks the stored content of a read that names no package at the address `packagelessAddress` resolves. That is the one resolution the package-less save, the package-less delete and the read's own `version` token already use (#23165). For an item whose active rows are bound to exactly one package `P`, the read serves what `?package=P` serves: `P`'s own row, else the package-unbound row (ADR-0048 prefer-local). Otherwise it serves any row, ADR-0048 §3.3's best-effort first match, as before. The strict draft read and the draft preview use the same address, because the package-less draft save inherits `P` from the active rows (#11087).

The change is content only. The lock layer is still selected at the address the `_lock` gate judges a package-less save at, so the read and the gate cannot bind different rows.

### Why (c)

- **(b) adopt was built first and measured wrong.** Commit `b776dcd1` made a write naming a package adopt the item's package-unbound row in `SysMetadataRepository.resolveWriteHead`, which generalizes the #11087 orphan-draft adoption. The full package suite went red in `protocol.org-scoped-write-refused.test.ts` (2 cases, "a package-less env-wide copy stands in for every package with no copy of its own"). Under ADR-0048 prefer-local, the package-unbound row is the **stand-in for every package that has no row of its own**. Adopting it into one package silently takes the customization away from every other package that read through it. That is a stored-data change the card does not authorize, and ADR-0070 calls this state a read-side detail, not one package's property. Commit `890bf1d3` reverts it.
- **(a) refuse** would narrow the save door (a save naming a package refused beside an unbound row). The author would also need a remedy: deleting the unbound row would remove the stand-in for every other package. (c) needs no new refusal and no remedy.
- **(c)** fits the wording of ADR-0070 TL;DR 1. The package-less state is no longer an authoring destination: every package-less write of a one-package item already goes to `P` since #23165. It stays "only as a read-side rehydration detail", and that is exactly what it remains here: the stand-in for packages with no row, and the row served again once `P`'s row is deleted. It also fixes a measured inconsistency inside the read itself. On `main`, the read naming no package served the unbound **body** with the package row's **`version` token** (HTTP reading below).
- **What (c) leaves:** the two rows stay stored (`[null, P]`). This is the residue the dispatch named for (c). No door reaches different rows through it any more. Whether to convert such pairs (a migration) is in Open questions.

## Measured first (mechanism assumptions)

**1. The card's five steps reproduce on `main`, at the protocol doors and over HTTP.**

At the protocol doors on `main` `90637274` (row-keeping engine double, the suite's own):
1. rows `[null]`;
2. rows `[[null,'unbound'],['com.qa.lanebapp','pkg']]`;
3. read naming none → `unbound`, read naming the package → `pkg`;
4. package-less save → `Saved app 's6' (env-wide, package=com.qa.lanebapp, state=active)`, read naming none → **`unbound`**, list → `['third']`;
5. package-less delete → `Deleted app 's6' (package=com.qa.lanebapp), and it still exists: its package-less row remains.`

Over HTTP on a real kernel (`pnpm dev:todo -- --fresh`, signed-in admin, SQLite), `PUT`/`GET`/`DELETE /api/v1/meta/app/NAME` with and without `?package=com.qa.lanebapp`. The `main` reading was taken with this PR's one-line fix ablated and the package rebuilt, with the dist preflight proving the ablated form was built:

| step | `main` (fix ablated) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 3 · GET, no package | label `unbound`, `version` = the package row's token | label `pkg`, `_packageId` `com.qa.lanebapp`, same token as `?package=` |
| 4 · PUT, no package, then GET, no package | receipt `package=com.qa.lanebapp`; GET serves **`unbound`** with the package row's token | receipt `package=com.qa.lanebapp`; GET serves `third` |
| 4 · list | `[["third","com.qa.lanebapp"]]` | `[["third","com.qa.lanebapp"]]` |
| 5 · DELETE, no package, then GET, no package | receipt "…its package-less row remains"; GET `unbound` | the same receipt; GET `unbound`, now the address of the next package-less save as well |

**2. How a package-less row comes to exist beside a package's row today.** Through today's doors, and not only from rows stored before ADR-0070. Step 1 (a package-less save of an item with no package binding writes the package-unbound row, #23165's control) followed by step 2 (a save naming the package inserts that package's row beside it) produces the pair on a fresh kernel, as the HTTP run shows. The other doors that write a `package_id`-null row only rewrite or promote a row already unbound: the server-stated rewrites (`source` set), the promotion of an unbound draft, and the restore of an unbound row. A save of a code-shipped item with no stored row writes the unbound overlay. Rows stored before ADR-0070 are a second source of the same pair, and the read handles both the same way.

## Pins

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packageless-save-address.test.ts`, a new `[#23291]` block on the suite's existing ledger-pinned engine double (no new double):

- **the card's five steps**, each read asserted against its save's address: after step 2 the read naming none serves `P`'s row with the same token as `?package=P`. Step 4's save, pinned to that token, is accepted and the read and the list serve it. Step 5's package-less delete leaves the unbound row, which the read and the next package-less save both address. A last package-less delete removes it with the original "it no longer exists" receipt;
- **storage order**: the unbound row stored first and second, both served as `P`'s;
- **the draft reads**: `?state=draft` and the draft preview serve `P`'s draft over an unbound draft, and the package-less draft save pinned to that token writes it;
- **edge, another package's row too** (`[null, P, Q]`, minted through the doors): package-less save and delete refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, nothing changed, each named read serves its own row. After `DELETE ?package=Q`, the read and the package-less save address `P` again;
- **control, the stand-in**: a read naming another package with no row still serves the unbound row (ADR-0048 prefer-local).

**Ablation** (fix committed first; `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor 1 → 0, blob `4ffc6d78` → `46991e7c`, restored blob = HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). With the resolution line deleted, **4 of the new pins go red**: five steps, unbound-row-first order, draft reads, edge. The unbound-row-second order and the stand-in control stay green, as controls should. The suite imports `./protocol.js` from source, so no dist leg applies. The HTTP `main` reading above used the same ablation with a rebuild: `ablation-dist-preflight` showed the marker absent, then present again after restore, and the tree clean.

## Verification (head `52bfacaa`, `origin/main` merged in at `73c7dc4a`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test`: 235 files passed, 3 skipped; 28395 tests passed, 19 skipped. `typecheck`: exit 0.
- `@objectstack/rest` real-route suites over this address family (`meta-draft-head-package-inheritance`, `meta-item-version-token-occ`, `meta-publish-package-scope`, `meta-item-envelope`, `meta-item-absent-404`, `meta-item-layered-route`): 82/82.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` reports "65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 64 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED". The one is `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`, exit 3, which refuses on a shallow clone (its positive control is pinned to a commit), so it is NOT MEASURED locally and CI runs it. `check:engine-double-contract` passed, since no new double was added.

## Changeset

`.changeset/23291-packageless-read-serves-save-address.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **patch**, `Clause-②: no`. No request is refused that was accepted, nothing new is accepted, no export or schema moves, and no stored row is rewritten. What changes is which stored row a `GET` naming no package serves in the two-row state. That is the defect, so it is not breaking.

## Open questions

- **Convert the `[null, P]` pair?** (c) leaves both rows stored. A migration could fold an unbound row into the package's when no other package reads through it. That is a stored-data decision and an ADR-0070 "migration source" step, out of this card's scope. Recommendation: no conversion unless a measured reader still reaches the wrong row.
- **The draft-save receipt** names no package when the draft inherits one (`(env-wide, state=draft)`), unlike the direct save's receipt. This was observed, not changed here.

## Acceptance notes

- `#23165` (option B, PR #23290) is untouched: the package-less save and delete still address the one package's row, and two packages are still refused.
- No other drafts holding `protocol.ts` were merged in. #23464 had landed on `main`, and `main` was merged before this PR opened (clean, delta vs `main` = the three files above).
